lead: Gilbert plumbing deals with very hard water, desert heat and mostly newer slab homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Gilbert.
risk: very hard water scale, water heaters worn out by minerals and slab leaks
risk_short: hard water, water heaters and slab leaks
why: Most Gilbert homes were built since the 1990s, so old pipe is less common than in Phoenix or Mesa. The big issues are minerals and age: the first water heaters, softeners and fixtures in these homes are wearing out.
Homes sit on slabs, so leaks under the floor happen. Summer heat in garages shortens water heater life.
water: Gilbert's water comes from the Salt and Verde rivers through SRP, Colorado River water through the Central Arizona Project and groundwater. It is very hard, so scale builds up quickly.
tips: Flush your water heater every year.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
areas: PipeMend works in the Heritage District, Agritopia, Val Vista Lakes, Power Ranch, Seville, Morrison Ranch and every other Gilbert neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the Town of Gilbert Development Services, and contractors need an Arizona Registrar of Contractors license.

faq.q: Do Gilbert homes need a water softener?
faq.a: Many homeowners add one. Gilbert's water is very hard, and scale shortens the life of water heaters, tankless units and fixtures. A water test helps size a softener.
